headline: A dragon story they can read all by themselves

pages.text: Under a tree sits a dragon. He is white, and his scales shine pink and green and blue.
The dragon looks up. A big tear wells up.
"I am Toby," he said. "I ran away from home."

title: Early chapter books for kids who can read them themselves: Julia and Toby
description: Julia finds a runaway dragon crying under a tree, and a beginning reader can read every word. Julia and Toby is a series of early chapter books for kids who have just learned to read, kindergarten to 2nd grade: a real fantasy story they can read on their own, with help on any word they get stuck on. Books for 6 year olds to read themselves, written with phonics and sight words. Free to read on any tablet, phone or computer. No ads, no account.

headline: Stuck on a word? Tap it.
sub: The sounds appear right there, so they keep reading on their own.
title: Stuck on a word? Tap it and its sounds appear: chapter books for beginning readers
description: In Julia and Toby, a beginning reader taps any word they are stuck on and its sounds appear in place: a dot under one letter, a bar under letter pairs like oo and er, just like phonics in class. Then they keep reading. It never reads the story to them. Decodable stories for kindergarten and 1st grade, with phonics and sight words. Free to read on any tablet, phone or computer. headline: When Toby gets mad, things fly

pages.text: Toby gets mad. His spikes stick up.
And then her dolls zoom up, high, high, high! Her drum zooms up. Her tea set zooms up!
Crash! Bang! Smash! They all come down.

headline: The magic rule: feelings make things float

pages.text: Sad: things float up, low and slow.
Mad: things zoom up high, then crash!
Glad: nothing floats at all. Or so Toby thinks...

title: A dragon whose feelings make things float: a fantasy chapter book for beginning readers
description: Tom, 12, gave his dragon one magic rule: Toby's feelings make things float. Sad, and they drift up slow. Mad, and everything zooms up and crashes. Happy, and nothing floats, or so Toby thinks. That's Julia and Toby, a fantasy series of early chapter books a kid who just learned to read can read alone. Dragon chapter books for kids, ages 5 to 7, kindergarten to 2nd grade. Free to read on any tablet, phone or computer. No ads, no account.

headline: Got a big kid who loves fantasy? Have them write one for the little one.
points: Start with one magic rule. Tom's: feelings make things float.
Use only words the little one can sound out.
End each chapter so they beg for the next.
title: Have your big kid write a story for the little one: how our 12-year-old wrote a dragon series
description: Our son Tom, 12, wrote a dragon series for his little sister, Yara, who had just learned to read.
